newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MALDINI SAYS ENGLAND COULD CRUSH ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALDINI SAYS ENGLAND COULD CRUSH ITALY.

text.p: Italy will be crushed by England in their World Cup qualifier next week if they simply rely on old-fashioned "catenaccio" defensive tactics, trainer Cesare Maldini said on Thursday.

Italy's new coach, known for his traditionally defensive brand of football, told reporters at the national training ground outside Florence that Italy faced a tough opponent at Wembley next Wednesday.

"The English game has changed compared to the stereotypes of the past -- they no longer play with just long passes. Their teams have a more organic game now, based more and more on physical performance," he said.

"Chelsea, Newcastle and Liverpool have a more complete game and the fact that the English have not won internationally for a while doesn't mean a thing: There's always a first time," added Maldini, whose son Paolo is captain of the national side.
"If we take the pitch at Wembley thinking we can simply 'contain' the English, they will crush us and slam us into our own goal.
"So we'll need to play with caution but we cannot give up (attacking) -- we'll have to play the kind of game that Italy knows how to play in these circumstances," he said.

Maldini, who led Italy's under-21 side to the last three European titles, hails from Italy's old school of soccer that preached "il catenaccio" (the bolt) -- defending in numbers and attacking on the counter-attack.
While not immune to changing tactics -- his junior sides occasionally played zone defence -- he prefers a traditional libero and two marking defenders.

In his debut last month -- a 2-0 win over Northern Ireland in a friendly -- he scrapped predecessor Arrigo Sacchi's zone and transformed his left-back son into a central marker and Juventus defender Ciro Ferrara into libero.
He said he was still not sure whether to field a 5-3-2 or a 4-4-2 formation against England.

"That's why I called up (Parma striker Enrico) Chiesa. I remembered that he played winger for Cremonese and could offer us an alternative on the right side of midfield to (Juventus's Angelo) Di Livio," Maldini said.
